clue.text: Hound a fellow from Kabul

blocks.note: first meaning: a long-haired breed of hunting dog
second meaning: a native of the capital's country

explanation.surface: Someone pestering a man who comes from the Afghan capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hound' reads as a verb, to harass, but it is a noun naming the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a tall silky-coated dog breed and any citizen of the nation whose capital is Kabul.

clue.text: Old car is quick and lively

blocks.note: first meaning: a family saloon made by Austin in the 1970s and 80s
second meaning: a musical tempo marking

explanation.surface: A vintage motor that still runs nippily.
explanation.walkthrough: The Austin Allegro was a British family car of the 1970s, now remembered mostly as a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the Italian tempo direction asks players to perform briskly and brightly; it also named a British Leyland model.

clue.text: Jealous kind of goddess

definitions.note: an adjective completing the phrase, not a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: envious, as with the colour of envy
second meaning: the word before 'goddess' in a salad dressing and an old army fire engine

explanation.surface: A deity of the envious sort, like Hera.
explanation.walkthrough: Green Goddess is a creamy herb salad dressing, and also the nickname of the British Army's old emergency fire engines.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is proverbially this colour, and the same colour word prefixes 'Goddess' in a dressing and a fire-engine nickname.

clue.text: At sea I ate man alive

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and all over the place, so the words that follow get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, seven letters to rework

explanation.surface: A castaway's grisly confession of cannibalism on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, the word means living or possessing life, as in animate versus inanimate objects.

clue.text: Vagrants trudge south

blocks.note: to tramp is to walk heavily
S is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: Homeless wanderers trudging southward along the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramps are homeless people who wander from place to place, which is exactly what vagrants are.

clue.text: Made response and created stir

indicators.note: to stir something is to mix it up, so the preceding word's letters get jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone answered back and caused a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Created stir' reads as 'caused a commotion', but 'stir' only mixes the letters of 'created'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have responded to something is to have behaved in reply, the past tense of react.

clue.text: Ship's officer takes foreign currency to obtain instruments

blocks.note: a mate is an officer on a merchant ship
rials are the currency of Iran and Oman

explanation.surface: A first mate changing money abroad to buy navigational instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes' simply joins the officer to the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment or tools needed for a task, such as writing materials, can loosely be called instruments.

clue.text: Partner's child puts his foot down

definitions.note: read as a two-word verb phrase

blocks.note: first meaning: a spouse's boy from an earlier relationship
second meaning: treads on something, split into two words

explanation.surface: A stepfather's lad finally asserts himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as STEPS ON, the answer literally describes putting a foot down; 'puts his foot down' pretends to mean laying down the law.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband's or wife's son from a previous marriage is that person's stepson, the child of one's partner.

clue.text: It goes badly for selfish type

indicators.note: something done badly comes out wrong, so the letters before it end up disordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Things turn out poorly for someone who thinks only of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: An egoist puts their own interests first, which makes them a self-centred person.

clue.text: Bedfellow who takes passive role

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the person

blocks.note: first meaning: whimsically, a partner who is asleep
second meaning: an investor in a business who has no part in running it

explanation.surface: A bed companion who lets the other take the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: In business, a partner who puts in money but takes no active part has this title; read literally it is a partner who is asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the standard British term for a silent investor, and literally describes someone dozing beside you.

clue.text: Programme shows woman concealing information

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside, so the woman's name wraps round the other piece

blocks.note: Ada is a woman's name
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A broadcast reveals a woman keeping facts secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is informal British for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be dealt with, a schedule or programme for a meeting.

clue.text: Good hobby

blocks.note: first meaning: benefit, as in acting for someone's good
second meaning: a pastime or pursuit one enjoys

explanation.walkthrough: 'Good' looks like an adjective praising the hobby, but it is a noun meaning advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means advantage or benefit, as in 'in your best interests', and also a leisure pursuit.

clue.text: See Steven cavorting in romantic hideaway

indicators.note: cavorting means leaping about wildly, so the name before it has its letters thrown around

blocks.note: lo is an old word for look or see, as in lo and behold
taken as written

explanation.surface: Catching Steven frolicking in a secret trysting place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See Steven' tempts as all anagram fodder, but that gives nine letters; 'See' supplies only LO.
explanation.definitionFit: A love nest is a cosy private place where lovers meet, a secret retreat for romance.

clue.text: Delighted to have access to daughter

blocks.note: an entrance is a way in
D is the standard abbreviation in family trees

explanation.surface: A parent thrilled to be allowed to visit their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone entranced is enchanted or spellbound, filled with wonder and great pleasure.

clue.text: Empties culverts

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, lets liquid run out of something
second meaning: a noun, channels carrying water under roads

explanation.walkthrough: 'Empties' reads like a noun, bottles, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for letting water flow away and a plural noun for underground water channels.

clue.text: He kills Mister Wild

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the title before it is scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A murder-story caption: a man named Mr Wild is the killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mister Wild' reads as a name, like Oscar Wilde; 'Wild' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiter is one who strikes down, especially fatally, so it is a man who kills.

clue.text: Playing Loman, he makes an entrance

indicators.note: playing means toying with, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor cast as Willy Loman walks onto the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Willy Loman is the hero of Arthur Miller's Death of a Salesman; 'makes an entrance' is theatre talk, but the answer is a literal hatchway.
explanation.definitionFit: A manhole is the covered opening giving workers a way down into a sewer or drain.

clue.text: Soldiers removing leader of tyrannical government

indicators.note: removing means taking away, so a letter is dropped from the soldiers' word
the leader of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: a regiment is a body of soldiers
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Troops overthrowing a despot's rule.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the T from the end of REGIMENT. Today the answer usually means a diet plan, but its older sense is rule or government.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen in its older sense is a system of rule or administration, which is a form of government.

clue.text: Urge chap to become a journalist

blocks.note: to press someone is to urge them
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Encouraging a fellow to take up reporting.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressman is someone who works for the newspapers, an old-fashioned word for a reporter.

clue.text: Clergyman quietly setting fire to building

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
arson is the crime of deliberately burning property

explanation.surface: A vicar stealthily torching a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson is a parish priest in the Church of England, a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Pitches tent and starts to explore nearby countryside with rough maps

rough means crude and unfinished, so the next word's letters are roughly rearranged

blocks.note: the opening letters of these three words
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hiker sets up camp and heads off into the countryside with crude maps.
explanation.definitionFit: To encamp is to settle in a camp, which means putting up tents for shelter.

clue.text: It's to be enjoyed freely any time

indicators.note: freely means without constraint, so the letters are free to move into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A slogan for a free facility you can use whenever you like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freely' looks like a promise that it costs nothing, but it marks the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An amenity is a pleasant or useful feature or facility, something provided for people's enjoyment.

clue.text: Object to nark being put at risk

blocks.note: an end is an aim or purpose
to nark is British slang for to irritate

explanation.surface: Protesting about a police informer whose safety is threatened.
explanation.walkthrough: A nark is British slang for a police informer, which the surface plays on; here it is the verb meaning to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger something is to expose it to harm or peril, placing it in jeopardy.

clue.text: Initially, Chinese teak's fashioned into a box

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word only
fashioned means shaped or made, so the wood's letters are worked into a new form

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
the word with its S

explanation.surface: Oriental hardwood being crafted into a chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A casket is a small ornamental chest for jewels or valuables, so it is a kind of box.

clue.text: System of locating some objects on a radar

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the last

explanation.surface: A technical description of how radar picks up objects.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites radar itself as the system, but the answer sits inside the words, a sound-based cousin.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonar uses sound pulses to detect and pinpoint underwater objects, a method of finding things.

clue.text: Unhappily, Ms Connie Tompson is of unsound mind

indicators.note: unhappily suggests things are not in a good state, so the name that follows is disordered

blocks.note: taken as written, all fifteen letters

explanation.surface: A sad report that a certain lady is mentally unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase is the legal term for someone not mentally competent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase literally means not in control of the mind, describing someone mentally incapable.

clue.text: Close friend in Glasgow provides a refuge

indicators.note: to provide a refuge is to shelter something inside, so the answer is tucked within the words

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word across the next two

explanation.surface: A best mate in Glasgow puts you up for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close friend' reads as one phrase, but 'Close' is the definition, a noun meaning the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The close of a story or event is its conclusion, the final part where it finishes.

clue.text: Duck's quarry is the fish-hawk

blocks.note: a duck is a cricket score of nought, O, with the S of the possessive
quarry is the hunted animal

explanation.surface: The bird that hunts ducks turns out to be the fish-hawk.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, so it stands for O.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a large raptor that dives for fish, long known by the name fish-hawk.
